title: Six Winters and One Short Note
subtitle: 工程建造 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 工程建造（人与社会·科学与技术）
meta: 主题语境：工程建造（人与社会·科学与技术）　|　核心词汇：estimate　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 estimate 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1967 my father ① made an estimate that no builder on the site would have accepted, and he said the making was the whole of the winter. The ② estimate, meaning the figure itself and not the plan, ran six winters and stayed unaccepted in the book; an estimate, he said, is the only thing on a site that is judged by how long it is left unaccepted.

Every ③ estimate on that site had the same short note beside it, and the ④ estimate at the far side, meaning the one they kept for the bridge and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. An estimate, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to accept; my father said the accepting is the part that fills six winters.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the estimate was the whole of the job, meaning the judgement and not the figure. The ⑥ estimate, meaning the judgement and not any of that, is the only thing in a job that everybody waits for and nobody accepts; estimate, he said, is either something you make or the only word that means both a figure and a judgement. He said the judgement is the part they remember.

By 1973 the ⑦ estimate had become a line in a report, and the report had become an argument about the short note. The ⑧ estimate of the whole thing, my father wrote in January, was one site and six winters of accepting; estimate, he said, is either the one at the far side or the reason you learned to accept. He said the accepting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ estimate I remember is the one accepted in the report, which closed in 1976 and is still described as the quietest on the site. An ⑩ estimate, my mother said in 1978, is the only one that improves by being accepted; every estimate, she said, is a judgement that has agreed to look like a figure. She said the judgement was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 估计；估算（指工地上每一份旁边的那一份）
B. n. 估算（指那个数字本身，与图样相对）
C. 固定搭配：make an estimate 作一次估算
D. n. 估算（指留给大桥的那一笔）

F. n. 估算（指报告上写到、被认可的那一份）
G. n. 判断；评价（指一项工程里人人都等却无人认可的那样东西）
H. n. 判断（抽象总称，指人人都等却无人认可的那样东西）

answers.why: make an estimate 意为“作一次估算”，1967 年父亲作了一份工地上没有一位施工者肯认可的估算。
estimate 意为“估算”，指那个数字本身而不是图样，它经过了六个冬天而在簿子上没有记号。
estimate 意为“估算”，指工地上每一份旁边的那一份，每一份旁边都有同一张短短的字条。
estimate 意为“估算”，指留给大桥的那一笔，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
estimate 意为“判断、评价”，指一项工程里人人都等却无人认可的那样东西，叔叔说这个判断就是那项工程活的全部。
estimate 意为“判断”，指人人都等却无人认可的那样东西而不是那个数字，是工程活里人人都等、却无人认可的东西。
estimate 意为“估算”，指报告上写到、被认可的那一份，到 1973 年这一份成了报告里的一行。
estimate 意为“估算”，父亲一月写道，整件事的估价之事是一处工地和六个冬天的认可。
estimate 意为“估算”，我记得的是报告上认可的那一份，1976 年结束了，至今仍被说成工地上最安静的一份。
estimate 为抽象总称，母亲 1978 年说，一份估算是唯一会因为被好好认可而变得更好的东西。
